options.content:
### Database DBM — deep ("Datadog-style") monitoring · targets the **F3 plane** (`$datname`, default `packiot_shadow`)
White-box Postgres + TimescaleDB internals: session saturation, throughput/efficiency, table & index health, the TimescaleDB automation plane (jobs / cagg lag / compression), and per-tenant load. Prometheus panels read postgres-exporter custom metrics; panels over catalog views not yet scraped read **native SQL against `packiot_shadow`** for immediate value (their exporter query is already in `queries.yaml`, so they migrate to Prometheus once it reloads). Switch `$datname` to `packiot` to inspect the legacy plane.

panels.title: Connection saturation
panels.description: sum(connections in $datname) / max_connections. The exporter emits pg_settings_max_connections (currently 50) — NOT hardcoded. Above ~0.8 = risk of 'too many clients'.

panels.title: Total connections
panels.description: sum(pg_activity_by_state_connections{datname=~"$datname"}) across all states.

panels.title: Idle-in-transaction age
panels.description: pg_activity_by_state_max_state_age_seconds{state="idle in transaction"} — age of the oldest idle-in-tx backend. The classic lock-holder / bloat cause.

panels.title: Longest active query
panels.description: pg_longest_query_longest_active_seconds — age of the longest currently-running statement. A climbing value = a stuck/heavy query.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: pg_activity_by_state_connections. Watch 'idle in transaction' — a sustained climb is a connection leak / un-closed txn.

panels.title: Transaction rate (commit vs rollback)
panels.description: rate(pg_db_activity_xact_commit[5m]) vs rollback. A rollback spike = errors upstream.

panels.title: Rollback ratio
panels.description: rollback / (commit + rollback). A rising ratio = a growing share of transactions aborting.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: pg_cache_hit_hit_ratio — buffer-cache hits / (hits + disk reads). Below ~0.98 sustained = memory pressure or a cold/heavy scan.

panels.title: Tuple activity (rate)
panels.description: rate(pg_db_activity_tup_*[5m]) — inserted/updated/deleted/fetched/returned. tup_returned >> tup_fetched = sequential-scan pressure.

panels.title: Deadlocks + temp-file spills (rate)
panels.description: rate(pg_db_activity_deadlocks[5m]) and rate(pg_db_activity_temp_bytes[5m]). Deadlocks should be flat 0; temp bytes = work_mem spills.

panels.title: Locks by mode (granted vs waiting)
panels.description: pg_locks_by_mode_granted (held) and _waiting (contention). pg_locks is cluster-global — no datname split. Any sustained 'waiting' = backends blocked.

options.content: #### Table / index health  ·  _native-SQL panels read `packiot_shadow` directly (F3); the matching exporter queries are in `queries.yaml` for later Prometheus migration_

panels.title: Top 25 tables by total size
panels.description: topk(25, pg_table_size_top_total_bytes{datname=~"$datname"}) — biggest relations (heap + indexes + TOAST).

panels.title: Dead-tuple ratio (bloat)
panels.description: pg_table_size_top_dead_tuples / clamp_min(pg_table_size_top_live_tuples, 1). High ratio = vacuum lag / bloat — a candidate for VACUUM or autovacuum tuning.

panels.title: Sequential-scan-heavy tables (native · F3)
panels.description: pg_stat_user_tables — rows read by sequential scans (missing-index smell). Native SQL over packiot_shadow now; exporter metric pg_stat_user_tables_seq_tup_read once Prometheus reloads.

targets.rawSql: SELECT schemaname AS schema, relname AS table, seq_scan, seq_tup_read, coalesce(idx_scan,0) AS idx_scan, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE schemaname NOT LIKE '\_timescaledb%' ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Unused / oversized indexes (native · F3)
panels.description: pg_stat_user_indexes — idx_scan=0 candidates for DROP, biggest first. Native SQL over packiot_shadow; exporter metric pg_stat_user_indexes_idx_scan later.

targets.rawSql: SELECT schemaname AS schema, relname AS table, indexrelname AS index, coalesce(idx_scan,0) AS idx_scan, pg_relation_size(indexrelid) AS size_bytes FROM pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE schemaname NOT LIKE '\_timescaledb%' ORDER BY coalesce(idx_scan,0) ASC, pg_relation_size(indexrelid) DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Autovacuum age + dead tuples (native · F3)
panels.description: pg_stat_user_tables — seconds since last autovacuum (-1 = never) and current dead-tuple count. Old vacuum + high dead tuples = bloat risk.

targets.rawSql: SELECT schemaname AS schema, relname AS table, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, CASE WHEN last_autovacuum IS NOT NULL THEN extract(epoch FROM now()-last_autovacuum)::bigint ELSE -1 END AS last_autovacuum_age_seconds, last_autovacuum FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE schemaname NOT LIKE '\_timescaledb%' ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Hypertables (size + chunks + compression)
panels.description: pg_timescaledb_hypertables_* — total size, chunk count, compression-enabled flag. Scoped to $datname, public schema.

panels.title: Continuous-aggregate refresh lag (native · F3)
panels.description: Seconds since each cagg's last successful refresh — the freshness of the OEE rollup plane. Native SQL over packiot_shadow; exporter metric pg_timescaledb_cagg_seconds_since_last_success later. -1 = no successful refresh on record.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ca.view_name AS cagg, CASE WHEN s.last_successful_finish IS NOT NULL AND isfinite(s.last_successful_finish) THEN extract(epoch FROM now()-s.last_successful_finish)::bigint ELSE -1 END AS seconds_since_last_success, s.last_run_status FROM timescaledb_information.continuous_aggregates ca LEFT JOIN timescaledb_information.jobs j ON j.hypertable_schema=ca.view_schema AND j.hypertable_name=ca.view_name AND j.proc_name='policy_refresh_continuous_aggregate' LEFT JOIN timescaledb_information.job_stats s ON s.job_id=j.job_id ORDER BY seconds_since_last_success DESC

panels.title: Background jobs status (native · F3)
panels.description: timescaledb_information.jobs + job_stats — last-run status, next start, cumulative failures. Native SQL over packiot_shadow; exporter metric pg_timescaledb_jobs_* later.

targets.rawSql: SELECT j.job_id, j.proc_name, coalesce(j.hypertable_name,'') AS hypertable, s.last_run_status, CASE WHEN s.next_start IS NOT NULL AND isfinite(s.next_start) THEN extract(epoch FROM s.next_start-now())::bigint ELSE NULL END AS seconds_to_next_start, coalesce(s.total_failures,0) AS total_failures, coalesce(s.total_runs,0) AS total_runs FROM timescaledb_information.jobs j LEFT JOIN timescaledb_information.job_stats s ON s.job_id=j.job_id ORDER BY coalesce(s.total_failures,0) DESC, j.job_id

panels.title: Compression effectiveness (native · F3)
panels.description: hypertable_compression_stats — before/after bytes, bytes saved, ratio (higher = better) per compressed hypertable. Native SQL over packiot_shadow; exporter metric pg_timescaledb_compression_* later.

targets.rawSql: SELECT h.hypertable_name AS hypertable, coalesce(cs.before_compression_total_bytes,0) AS before_bytes, coalesce(cs.after_compression_total_bytes,0) AS after_bytes, coalesce(cs.before_compression_total_bytes,0)-coalesce(cs.after_compression_total_bytes,0) AS saved_bytes, CASE WHEN coalesce(cs.after_compression_total_bytes,0)>0 THEN round((cs.before_compression_total_bytes::numeric/cs.after_compression_total_bytes),1) ELSE 0 END AS ratio FROM timescaledb_information.hypertables h LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM hypertable_compression_stats(format('%I.%I',h.hypertable_schema,h.hypertable_name))) cs ON true WHERE cs.after_compression_total_bytes IS NOT NULL ORDER BY saved_bytes DESC

options.content:
#### Top / slow queries — ⏳ PENDING `pg_stat_statements`
This section lights up once the `pg_stat_statements` extension is enabled. **Prereqs (out of scope for this dashboard PR — separate scheduled task):**
1. Add `pg_stat_statements` to `shared_preload_libraries` in the TimescaleDB config.
2. **Restart the database** (required — `shared_preload_libraries` is not runtime-settable).
3. `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;` in each monitored DB.
4. Add a `pg_stat_statements` block to `monitoring/postgres-exporter/queries.yaml` (or a native-SQL panel over `packiot-postgres-shadow`).

**Intended queries once available** (native SQL over `packiot_shadow`):
```sql
-- Top 25 by total execution time
SELECT queryid, calls, round(total_exec_time) AS total_ms,
       round(mean_exec_time, 2) AS mean_ms, rows,
       round(100.0 * shared_blks_hit /
             nullif(shared_blks_hit + shared_blks_read, 0), 1) AS hit_pct,
       left(query, 120) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 25;

-- Top 25 by mean latency (slowest per call, calls > 10)
SELECT queryid, calls, round(mean_exec_time, 2) AS mean_ms,
       round(stddev_exec_time, 2) AS stddev_ms, left(query, 120) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements
WHERE calls > 10
ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 25;

-- Top 25 by temp-block spill (work_mem pressure)
SELECT queryid, calls, temp_blks_written, temp_blks_read,
       left(query, 120) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements
WHERE temp_blks_written > 0
ORDER BY temp_blks_written DESC
LIMIT 25;
```

panels.title: Worker batch writes by tenant (F3)
panels.description: rate(oeecloud_worker_batch_writes_total{dest="f3_packiot_shadow", result="ok"}[5m]) by tenant — write pressure the F3 plane carries per tenant.

panels.title: HTTP request rate by service (job)
panels.description: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) by job — API-tier load hitting the DB behind each service.
